purpose: Select which already-true scene facts must remain visibly legible after style and brush translation.

required.instruction: At least one unfinished work must visibly expose raw ground or underpainting beneath only partially developed pigment.
At least one painted passage must visibly stop before reaching the edge of its support, leaving the interruption clearly legible.
At least one surface must visibly preserve erased, revised, overwritten, or partially removed marks.
At least one wall area must visibly retain a faint prior hanging trace such as a tonal rectangle, nail mark, or placement ghost.

compositionControls.instruction: An empty frame may appear, but it must remain one element among multiple unfinished processes and must not become the dominant shorthand for the room.
Distribute visual attention across several materially different states of incompletion rather than organizing the room around one centered hero frame.
Keep the hanging field visibly irregular in spacing, completion, and alignment while remaining plausible as an inhabited gallery.

reviewQuestions: Can a viewer point to visible underpainting or raw ground?
Can a viewer point to an interrupted or revised painted passage?
Can a viewer point to evidence that a work or frame previously occupied another position?
Does unfinishedness read as process rather than blankness?
